analysis:
Examined the only change in StandaloneServer.swift: head hunks near lines 1538-1564 (the patch shows them; the head text unit covers only lines 1-587, so the changed region is seen through the patch excerpt, not as numbered head lines). The change adds a one-time reclaim step in the memory-headroom wait loop (ensureMemoryHeadroomForLoad). Before evicting an LRU idle model, it now calls the new releaseReclaimableMemoryForLoad(). That method calls GlobalKVCacheBudget.releaseRetainedKVSegments() and then MLX.Memory.clearCache() when nativeMiMoReclaimAllowed. The step is skipped when no busy engines keep reclaimable memory.

Security assessment: this is a local memory-management and availability optimization in the standalone/local server. It adds no new input surface, auth path, network or coordinator interaction, key handling, or plaintext logging. It is relevant to T-028 (residual GPU memory) and T-010/T-029 availability, and it only releases more memory, so it does not weaken them. Releasing retained KV segments and clearing the MLX cache can only reduce residual data. The loop is bounded: poolDropped flips once, then it either evicts or throws capacityUnavailable. Task cancellation is still checked each iteration. The load-gate serialization (isLoadingAny) still wraps the call path, per the base load function at lines 1833-1847.

Unverified contracts: GlobalKVCacheBudget.releaseRetainedKVSegments() and busyEnginesKeepReclaimableMemory() are defined in unchanged or other files outside this batch. I could not check whether releaseRetainedKVSegments can free segments still referenced by in-flight requests, or whether it can stall under actor contention. Its comment says it waits briefly. The prefix-cache staging reservations in T-041 are not touched in the supplied diff. No finding is supported by the visible evidence.
